content.title: [Tech Debt]: Remove silent config fallback — make --config mandatory
content.body:
### Problem

The server silently falls back to `.github/scrum/config.yml` when no `--config` flag or `SCRUM_CONFIG_PATH` env var is provided. When that default path doesn't exist, the server starts in "degraded mode" with stub tools — every tool call returns `"Config not found"` instead of crashing at startup with a clear error.

This masks a genuine configuration error. A developer who starts from the wrong directory or without knowing the flag sees a running process that does nothing useful.

### Diagnosis

**Layer 1 — Server** (`src/server.ts:117-121`): `_configLocation: ContentLocation | undefined` — becomes `undefined` when no config source is provided. The type itself lies.

**Layer 2 — Adapter** (`src/adapters/github/config-loader.ts:360-363`): `params.configLocation ?? { kind: "file", path: resolve(Deno.cwd(), ".github/scrum/config.yml") }` — a hidden default path.

**Cascade — ConfigReloader** (`src/adapters/github/internal/config-reloader.ts:19`): calls `loadConfig({ github: this.github })` without `configLocation` — will silently break if the `??` fallback is removed without updating this site.

### Impact if not fixed

- **Bad UX:** Server starts without error but every tool fails silently
- **Hidden coupling:** The adapter embeds a default path that only works when CWD is the project root
- **Type debt:** `ContentLocation | undefined` propagates through 5 function/interface signatures where the value is actually always required

### Implementation — 11 sites, 6 files

1. `src/server.ts:114-121` — Add `if (!_rawConfigPath) { console.error(); Deno.exit(1); }`
2. `src/server.ts:78-87` — Help text: remove "(default: .github/scrum/config.yml)", add "(required)"
3. `src/server.ts:245-247` — `createMcpServer(configLocation?:)` → `(configLocation:)`
4. `src/server.ts:262-277` — Simplify error branches (remove dead `else if` / `else`)
5. `src/server.ts:339-341` — `runStdio(configLocation?:)` → `(configLocation:)`
6. `src/server.ts:366` — `runHttp(configLocation?:)` → `(configLocation:)`
7. `src/adapters/factory.ts:18-23` — `AdapterStartupOptions.configLocation` required
8. `src/adapters/github/config-loader.ts:72-77` — `ConfigParams.configLocation` required
9. `src/adapters/github/config-loader.ts:360-363` — Remove `??` fallback
10. `src/adapters/github/internal/config-reloader.ts:12-19` — Add `configLocation` param
11. `src/adapters/github/factory.ts:119` — Pass `configLocation` to `ConfigReloader`

### What stays

- `registerStubTools()` — still needed for `AUTH_FAILED` degraded mode
- `SCRUM_CONFIG_PATH` — still supported (now mandatory)
- The `try/catch` around `createBackend` — needed for other adapter errors

Full plan: `plans/remove-config-fallback.md`

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Server exits with code 1 and clear message when no `--config` or `SCRUM_CONFIG_PATH` set
- [ ] All `ContentLocation | undefined` signatures updated to `ContentLocation` (no lying optionality)
- [ ] `ConfigReloader.reload()` correctly passes the original config location
- [ ] Help text shows `--config` as required
- [ ] `registerStubTools` still works for `AUTH_FAILED` errors

content.title: [Tech Debt]: Consolidate sprint date math and remove dead functions in `sprint-math.ts`
content.body:
## Debt Description

### Part A — Dead functions (from #109)

Two functions in [`src/scrum/sprint-math.ts`](src/scrum/sprint-math.ts) have **zero importers**:

- `computeSprintTotals` (line 53) — never called by any use case
- `groupStoriesByStatus` (line 90) — never called by any use case

The [`get-sprint.ts`](src/scrum/get-sprint.ts) file computes `by_status` inline (lines 77-81) and `story_points` via `reduce` (line 105) instead of using these functions.

### Part B — Duplicated sprint date math (from #114)

Sprint date computation is duplicated in **three places** with slightly different implementations:

1. [`src/scrum/sprint-math.ts:26-28`](src/scrum/sprint-math.ts:26) — `buildSprintMeta()`: Uses local-time `setDate`/`setHours`
2. [`src/scrum/sprint-math.ts:127-130`](src/scrum/sprint-math.ts:127) — `buildSprintWindow()`: Uses UTC `setUTCDate`/`setUTCHours(0,0,0,0)`
3. [`src/adapters/github/mappers.ts:288-289`](src/adapters/github/mappers.ts:288) — `toSprintInfo()`: Same logic again

The inconsistency between local-time and UTC methods could cause **off-by-one errors around timezone boundaries**.

## Cost of Deferral

- Timezone-related bugs may surface unpredictably
- Three implementations to maintain — any fix must be applied in three places
- Dead code creates false confidence — a developer might assume these are used and modify them
- Risk of divergence between the local-time and UTC versions

## Proposed Improvement

1. Delete `computeSprintTotals` and `groupStoriesByStatus` from `sprint-math.ts`. If needed, restore from git history.
2. Consolidate sprint date computation into a single function in `sprint-math.ts`. Both `toSprintInfo()` and `buildSprintMeta()` should delegate to it. Choose a consistent time approach (UTC recommended).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `computeSprintTotals` and `groupStoriesByStatus` removed from `sprint-math.ts`
- [ ] Single source of truth for sprint date computation in `sprint-math.ts`
- [ ] `buildSprintMeta()` delegates to the consolidated function
- [ ] `toSprintInfo()` in `mappers.ts` delegates to the consolidated function
- [ ] Consistent time approach (UTC or local) applied everywhere
- [ ] No other files reference the removed functions (confirmed via search)
- [ ] No behavioral change — existing tests pass
- [ ] `deno lint` passes with no errors
- [ ] `deno test` passes

## Notes

- Findings 4 + 23 from Clean Code Audit (2026-05-20)
- Smell codes: G5 (Duplication), G33 (Timezone inconsistency), G9 (Dead code)
- **MERGED**: Absorbed story #109 on 2026-05-21 — both target `sprint-math.ts` cleanup

content.title: Per-connection config override in SSE mode
content.body:
# 📖 User Story: Per-connection config override in SSE mode

## As a…

A client connecting to a shared SSE server

## I want…

To pass my own config file path in the MCP `initialize` handshake

## So that…

I can use my project-specific Scrum config while sharing server infrastructure with other teams.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A client may pass `{ "meta": { "configPath": "<path>" } }` in the `initialize` request
- [ ] The server resolves `configPath` against its own filesystem (not the client's); the path must be accessible to the server process
- [ ] The per-connection config **fully replaces** the server's default config for that session — no merging
- [ ] If `configPath` is provided but the file is missing or fails to parse, the connection is rejected with a descriptive error; other sessions are unaffected
- [ ] If `configPath` is absent, the session uses the server's startup default config
- [ ] `FileReaderPort` for the session is scoped to the directory of the session's resolved config file
- [ ] Backend credentials come from server environment variables only; the per-connection config file must not embed tokens
- [ ] "Full override" semantics and the credential restriction are documented

## Story Point Estimate

3

## Affected component

MCP tool surface (scrum_* tools)

### Dependencies
- **Depends on:** #93 (Run the server in SSE mode — SSE transport must exist before per-connection overrides can be layered on)
- **Unblocks:** nothing

### 7. Unused parameter

## Root cause

Design drift during the EpicRef migration (Phase 2 of the Epic & Dependency System). The old milestone title-to-ID resolution path was superseded by direct `MI_` node ID passing, but the dead code was never cleaned up. The EpicRef migration story (#102) focused on adding the new path, not removing the old one.

Dead code accumulates and confuses future readers. The explicit `// TODO: dead` tag means every developer who reads that file wastes time wondering whether to clean it up. Execute all 7 items in dependency order:

1. Remove dead `resolveOrCreateMilestoneNodeId` method + supporting internal types from `user-milestone-resolver.ts`

6. Remove stale TODO comment from `types.ts` (Option A: the flat interface pattern is maintainable as-is)
7. Remove unused `_fileReader` parameter from `scrum-read.ts` and its call site in `server.ts`

Full execution plan: `plans/adapter-cleanup-plan.md`

- [ ] `deno lint` passes (no dangling imports or unused variables)
- [ ] `deno task test` passes (no broken references to deleted fixtures)
- [ ] No `import` statements reference `GET_USER_MILESTONES_QUERY` or `CREATE_MILESTONE_MUTATION`

content.title: [Tech Debt]: Update agent behavioral rules for the redesigned tool surface
content.body:
## Problem statement

The agent rules in `.roo/` still reference the old tool surface: `scrum_get_sprint`, `scrum_get_backlog`, `scrum_get_story`, `scrum_get_burndown`, `scrum_get_history`, and `scrum_get_template`. The session start protocol unconditionally calls `scrum_get_backlog` regardless of task type, and the rules contain no guidance on direct item lookup, dependency graph usage, or task-driven health loading.

## Root cause

The rules were written against the original tool surface and have not been updated to reflect the redesign. Behavioral guidance is encoded in rules files, not inferred from tool descriptions alone.

## Affected architectural layer

Agent mode (`.roo/`)

## Risk if deferred

Even with the new tools shipped, the agent will fall back to old patterns — full board dumps for single-ticket requests, unconditional health loads on every session, no use of the dependency graph opt-in — defeating the performance and clarity goals of the entire epic.

## Proposed approach

### 1. Update session start protocol
`scrum_orient` → gap check → classify and route. Remove unconditional `scrum_get_backlog` call.

Encode task-driven health-loading table:

| Session type | Load board health? |
|---|---|
| Planning / refinement / retrospective / ambiguous | Yes → `scrum_get_board_health` |
| Single item lookup or targeted write on named item | No |

### 2. Encode sprint risk stance from orient (pre-computed)

`scrum_orient` returns `platform_state.iterations.active.riskStance` as a pre-computed field.
**Do not recompute it from `time_elapsed_pct` alone.**

The server computes it as `time_elapsed_pct / work_pct` ratio:
- `normal` — time ≤ 110% of work completed
- `monitor` — time between 110–130% of work completed
- `elevated` — time ≥ 130% of work completed, or time > 0 with no work done

Agent rule: read `riskStance` from orient; act on `normal` / `monitor` / `elevated` directly.

### 3. Encode direct lookup pattern

- **Single item full detail** (body, comments, AC, linked PRs): `scrum_get_item_detail(ref: { number: N })`
- **Multi-item listing** by issue numbers: `scrum_find_items(keys: ["42", "123"])` — keys are **numeric string arrays**
- Never dump the full board to resolve a human-readable reference.

### 4. Encode `scope` vs `sprint_ref` distinction for `scrum_find_items`

Two overlapping sprint filters with different semantics:
- `scope: "sprint"` — returns items whose sprint = the current active sprint (platform's `state.iterations.active`)
- `sprint_ref: "<name>"` — filters by a specific named sprint (any sprint, including completed)

Use `scope: "sprint"` for "what's in the current sprint"; use `sprint_ref` for retrospective or cross-sprint queries.

### 5. Encode impediment lookup pattern

`scrum_get_board_health` returns `impediments: { open_count, orphan_count }` — **counts only, no refs**.
To get actual impediment listings or refs: `scrum_find_items(types: ["impediment"])`.

Replace current rule `scrum_get_backlog labels:["impediment"]` with:
- Health check → `scrum_get_board_health` (counts)
- Logging impediments / linking to items → `scrum_find_items(types: ["impediment"])` (listings with refs)

### 6. Encode template resource access with guard

`scrum_get_template` is removed. Templates are now MCP resources at `scrum://template/{type}`.

Guard required: `templateResourceUseCase` throws if the type is not declared in `typeTemplatePaths`.
Before accessing a template resource, check `platform_state.template_uris` from `scrum_orient`.
Only access `scrum://template/{type}` for types present in that map.

### 7. Encode dependency graph decision table

Fetch-or-skip signals from unresolved `DependencyNode` entries (`resolved: false` in the dependency map returned by `scrum_find_items(include_dependencies: true)`).

### 8. Remove all references to removed tools

Remove: `scrum_get_sprint`, `scrum_get_backlog`, `scrum_get_burndown`, `scrum_get_history`, `scrum_get_template`, `scrum_get_story`.

### 9. Fix schema docstring bugs in `src/schemas/scrum.ts` (additional scope)

Three incorrect docstrings discovered during implementation audit — these are agent-visible via JSON Schema and cause incorrect behavior independent of the rules update:

- **`SprintRefSchema` description**: references `scrum_get_sprint` (removed). Update to reference `scrum_find_items`.
- **`UpdateStorySchema.body` describe**: says `"Call scrum_get_story first"`. Update to `scrum_get_item_detail`.
- **`UpdateImpedimentSchema.ref.id` describe**: says `"scrum_get_board_health.impediments[].ref.id"` — but `BacklogHealth.impediments` only has `{ open_count, orphan_count }`, no `.ref.id`. Update to `"scrum_find_items(types: ['impediment']).items[].ref.id"`.

## Done criteria

- [ ] No reference to `scrum_get_sprint`, `scrum_get_backlog`, `scrum_get_burndown`, `scrum_get_history`, `scrum_get_template`, or `scrum_get_story` in `.roo/`
- [ ] Session start protocol updated with task-driven health-loading table
- [ ] `riskStance` stance table encodes pre-computed field from orient (not a `time_elapsed_pct` threshold table)
- [ ] Direct lookup pattern encoded: `scrum_get_item_detail` for single item; `scrum_find_items(keys: [...])` for multi-item listings
- [ ] `scope` vs `sprint_ref` distinction encoded in rules
- [ ] Impediment lookup pattern encoded: health counts via `scrum_get_board_health`; listings/refs via `scrum_find_items(types: ["impediment"])`
- [ ] Template resource guard encoded: check `platform_state.template_uris` before accessing `scrum://template/{type}`
- [ ] Dependency graph pattern encoded
- [ ] All new tool names (`scrum_find_items`, `scrum_get_item_detail`, `scrum_get_board_health`, `scrum_get_analytics`) referenced correctly
- [ ] Schema docstring bugs fixed in `src/schemas/scrum.ts` (3 items listed above)

Agent consuming `scrum_orient`

## I want…
`platform_state.epics.active` to contain a list of `EpicSummary` entries scoped to the current sprint, plus a `total_count`

## So that…
I have thematic context for prioritization and sequencing after a single orient call, without needing a separate epic listing call

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `platform_state.epics.active` returns epics that have ≥1 item assigned to the active sprint, each with `id`, `name`, `description`, and `open_item_count`
- [ ] `platform_state.epics.total_count` is always populated regardless of sprint state

content.title: [Bug]: Board item comments land on wrong GitHub issue when project spans multiple repositories
content.body:
## Expected behaviour

When `scrum_update_story` posts a comment on a project board item, the comment appears on the GitHub issue that the board item represents — matching the board item's displayed title and content.

## Actual behaviour

The comment is posted to the underlying GitHub issue that the board item is *linked* to, which may belong to a different repository on the same project board. If the board item's link points to a cross-repo issue, the comment silently lands there instead.

**Observed instance:** The project board item titled "Impediment: The `scrum_update_story` tool is currently failing with a GraphQL error" (PVTI `PVTI_lAHOAmfLjc4BWiTtzgs66F4`) has its underlying GitHub issue link pointing to `MesseBuddy/issues/13` ("Story B: Backend Abstraction Layer (Phase 5)") — a different repository. A comment intended for the impediment was posted to `MesseBuddy/issues/13` instead, with no warning or error returned by the tool.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Add a project board item from repository A to a GitHub Projects board that also contains items from repository B
2. Ensure the board item's displayed title/content diverges from the linked GitHub issue in repo B
3. Call `scrum_update_story` with a `comment` on that board item's project item ID
4. Observe the comment appears on the unrelated issue in repo B, not on the expected item

## Affected MCP tool

- scrum_update_story

## Severity

Major – incorrect output, workaround exists

## Additional context

The root cause is that GitHub Projects v2 board items can be linked to issues from any repository in the organisation. The `scrum_update_story` comment path follows the linked GitHub issue node ID without validating that it belongs to the expected repository. The board item display title is stored separately on the project item and can differ from the linked issue's actual title, making the mismatch invisible to the caller.

**Workaround:** Verify the `url` field returned by `scrum_get_story` matches the expected repository before posting a comment.

---

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `scrum_update_story` detects when the linked GitHub issue belongs to a repository other than the primary project repository (from config) and warns the caller before posting
- [ ] The warning includes the linked issue's actual URL and title so the caller can make an informed decision
- [ ] Alternatively: the tool documentation clearly states that comments are posted to the linked GitHub issue, not to the project board item display, and `scrum_get_story` always surfaces the `url` prominently in its response

content.title: [Tech Debt]: Fix FieldValueMutator — GitHubClient adoption and parameterized mutations
content.body:
## Problem statement

`FieldValueMutator` has two independent defects:

1. **Type inconsistency** — `gh` is typed `typeof graphql` (a bare function) and is called as `this.gh(query, vars)`. All other services use the object-wrapper form `this.gh.graphql(...)`. This is inconsistent and incompatible with `GitHubClient`.
2. **String interpolation in mutations** — All five field-setting mutations interpolate values directly into the GraphQL string instead of using named variables, creating an injection risk and losing type safety on responses.

## Root cause

`FieldValueMutator` was written before the `GitHubClient` interface existed. String interpolation was used as the path of least resistance during initial implementation.

## Affected architectural layer

GitHub adapter (src/adapters/github/)

## Risk if deferred

- String interpolation in GraphQL mutations is a security risk if any value is externally influenced
- Inconsistent `gh` typing makes the codebase harder to reason about and blocks transport-layer improvements
- No typed generics on mutation responses means errors in the response shape go undetected at compile time

## Proposed approach

1. Update `gh` field to `GitHubClient`; replace all `this.gh(...)` bare calls with `this.gh.graphql(...)`
2. Parameterize all five mutation methods (`setFieldStatus`, `setFieldSprint`, `setFieldStoryPoints`, `setFieldPriority`, `setFieldAssignee`) with named GraphQL variables and typed response generics
3. Leave `clearField` paths unchanged — they already use parameterized variables

## Done criteria

- [ ] `FieldValueMutator.gh` is typed `GitHubClient`; all calls use `this.gh.graphql(...)`
- [ ] All five mutation methods use named GraphQL variables — no string interpolation in mutation bodies
- [ ] All mutations have typed response generics
- [ ] `clearField` continues to use parameterized variables (no regression)
- [ ] `deno check` passes

The use-case layer currently depends on the full `ProjectBackend` interface, which includes methods that are not required by every use case (e.g., file system operations). This violates the Interface Segregation Principle (ISP).

## Root cause

During initial development, a monolithic `ProjectBackend` was used for simplicity. As the project matured and specialized ports were introduced, the use cases were not updated to use these narrower interfaces.

## Scope

- Violates ISP and makes the architecture more fragile.
- Makes it harder to swap out or mock specific parts of the backend for testing.
- Increases coupling between the use-case layer and the full adapter implementation.

## Solution approach

1. For each use case file in `src/scrum/`, identify the minimum set of methods required from the backend.
2. Import the corresponding focused port(s) from `src/scrum/ports.ts`.
3. Update the function signatures to use these narrow ports instead of `ProjectBackend`.
4. Verify that all use cases still compile and pass `deno check`.

content.title: [Bug]: Backlog field data missing for all items; label mutations silently fail on Draft Issues
content.body:
## Expected behaviour

- `scrum_get_backlog` returns correct `status`, `story_points`, and `priority` values for all items — both Draft Issues and regular Issues.
- `scrum_update_story` with a `labels` update on a Draft Issue applies the labels transparently, auto-converting the Draft Issue to a full GitHub Issue when necessary.

## Actual behaviour

### Problem 1 — Backlog listing returns null for all board fields

Every item returned by `scrum_get_backlog` shows `status: null`, `story_points: null`, `priority: null`.

`StoryQueryService.getBacklogStories()` passes `sprintFieldIds` to `PaginatedProjectItemFetcher`, triggering a query optimisation in `pagination.ts` that only renders `ProjectV2ItemFieldIterationValue` sub-fields. All other field-value node types (`ProjectV2ItemFieldSingleSelectValue`, `ProjectV2ItemFieldNumberValue`) return as bare `{ __typename }` with no value fields. `extractBoardFields` finds nothing to extract.

### Problem 2 — Label and comment mutations throw on Draft Issues

`scrum_update_story` with `labels`, `scrum_update_story` with `assignees`, and `addComment` all throw `DRAFT_ISSUE_CONSTRAINT` on Draft Issues. Draft Issues have no backing GitHub Issue node, so any mutation that targets an Issue node ID fails.

## Steps to reproduce

**Problem 1:**
1. Call `scrum_get_backlog`
2. Observe `status: null`, `story_points: null`, `priority: null` on every returned item

**Problem 2:**
1. Identify a Draft Issue on the board
2. Call `scrum_update_story` with `labels: ["bug"]` on that item
3. Observe `DRAFT_ISSUE_CONSTRAINT` error

## Affected MCP tool

- scrum_get_backlog (Problem 1)
- scrum_update_story (Problem 2)

## Severity

Major – incorrect output, workaround exists

## Additional context

Discovered during Sprint 1 board health diagnostics (2026-05-15), follow-on to #32.

**Fix for Problem 1:** Remove `sprintFieldIds` from the backlog fetcher options. `isBacklogItem` still works correctly with the full field fragment since sprint iteration nodes remain present or absent regardless.

**Fix for Problem 2:** In `StoryMutationService`, before any operation requiring a backing Issue node, if `resolved.issueId === null`, call `convertProjectV2DraftIssueItemToIssue` with the item ID and repository node ID (available via `labelResolver.fetchRepoNodeId()`), then use the returned Issue ID for the mutation.

```graphql
mutation ConvertDraftIssue($itemId: ID!, $repositoryId: ID!) {
  convertProjectV2DraftIssueItemToIssue(input: {
    itemId: $itemId
    repositoryId: $repositoryId
  }) {
    item { id content { ... on Issue { id number } } }
  }
}
```

---

## Acceptance Criteria

### Field data (Problem 1)
- [ ] `scrum_get_backlog` returns correct `status`, `story_points`, and `priority` values for regular Issues
- [ ] `scrum_get_backlog` returns correct `status`, `story_points`, and `priority` values for Draft Issues
- [ ] `isBacklogItem` still correctly filters out sprint-assigned items (no regression)
- [ ] `deno check src/index.ts` passes

### Draft Issue auto-conversion (Problem 2)
- [ ] Calling `scrum_update_story` with `labels` on a Draft Issue converts it to a full Issue transparently and applies the labels
- [ ] Calling `scrum_update_story` with `assignees` on a Draft Issue converts and assigns
- [ ] Calling `addComment` on a Draft Issue converts and posts the comment
- [ ] The conversion uses `convertProjectV2DraftIssueItemToIssue` — the project item ID is preserved; only the content type changes
- [ ] If conversion fails, a clear `GitHubApiError` is thrown with recovery guidance
- [ ] Draft Issues only having project-board fields set (`status`, `sprint`, `story_points`, `priority`) are **not** converted — those mutations work on the project item ID directly
- [ ] `deno check src/index.ts` passes

User input (`login`) is passed to the GitHub GraphQL API as a named variable, not interpolated into the query string. Special characters in usernames do not break the query, and attacker-controlled input cannot alter the query structure.

## Actual behaviour

`resolveUserNodeId()` interpolates `login` directly into the query string:

```graphql
query { user(login: "${login}") { id } }
```

A username containing `"` or other special characters breaks the query syntax. If attacker-controlled input reaches this function, the query structure can be altered.

**Location:** [`src/adapters/github/backend.ts:374`](src/adapters/github/backend.ts#L374)

## Steps to reproduce

1. Trigger any tool that resolves a user node ID (e.g. `scrum_update_story` with an `assignees` value, or `scrum_create_story` with assignees)
2. Supply a username containing a special character such as `user"name` or `user'name`
3. Observe a malformed GraphQL query error or unexpected query behaviour

## Affected MCP tool

- scrum_update_story
- scrum_create_story

## Severity

Major – incorrect output, workaround exists

---

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Refactor `resolveUserNodeId()` to use GraphQL variables instead of string interpolation
- [ ] Change query from `` `query { user(login: "${login}") { id } }` `` to `` `query GetUser($login: String!) { user(login: $login) { id } }` `` with variable injection
- [ ] Verify no regressions with `deno test`
- [ ] Test with special-character usernames: `user'o"b`, `user-name`, `user_name`

TypeScript interface segregation at the service level means: accept the narrowest possible collaborator type, not a concrete class. An alternative — and simpler — solution is to pass the already-resolved `repoNodeId` as a constructor parameter. Since the server is stateless and each invocation calls `loadConfig`, the repo node ID is stable within a request. ## Story Point Estimate
5

## Affected component
GitHub adapter (src/adapters/github/)

## Additional context / notes
### Why: GraphQL variable parameterization — security and type safety
Embedding IDs in mutation strings via template literals bypasses GraphQL's type system. The GitHub GraphQL API enforces `ID!` types on input fields — sending a mis-formed string in an interpolated mutation produces a runtime error with no compile-time signal. Using named variables (`$itemId: ID!`) lets the API validate the type at the protocol level and gives the TypeScript generic `<ResponseType>` meaningful structure. It also eliminates the possibility of structural injection if any ID value ever comes from untrusted input.

The `clearField` method already uses parameterized variables correctly — apply the same pattern to the five remaining mutation methods.

### Implementation Steps
**Step 1 — Update `gh` field type**
- Change `private readonly gh: typeof graphql` to `private readonly gh: GitHubClient`
- Update the constructor parameter to `gh: GitHubClient`
- Replace all call sites of `this.gh(query, vars)` (bare function) with `this.gh.graphql(query, vars)`
- Import `GitHubClient` from `./http-client.ts`; remove the `graphql` function import

**Step 2 — Parameterize `setFieldStatus`**
- Remove the template literal mutation string
- Replace with a named operation `SetFieldStatus` with variables `$projectId: ID!`, `$itemId: ID!`, `$fieldId: ID!`, `$optionId: String!`
- Add typed generic: `this.gh.graphql<{ updateProjectV2ItemFieldValue: { item: { id: string } } }>(...)`
- Pass `{ projectId: this.config.projectId, itemId, fieldId, optionId }` as the variables object

**Step 3 — Parameterize `setFieldSprint`**
- Named operation: `SetFieldSprint` with variables `$projectId: ID!`, `$itemId: ID!`, `$fieldId: ID!`, `$iterationId: String!`
- Value type for iteration: `value: { iterationId: $iterationId }` in the mutation
- The `clearField` path (when `iterationId === null`) already uses parameterized variables — leave it as-is

**Step 4 — Parameterize `setFieldStoryPoints`**
- Named operation: `SetFieldStoryPoints` with variables `$projectId: ID!`, `$itemId: ID!`, `$fieldId: ID!`, `$number: Float!`
- Note: GitHub Projects v2 uses `Float!` (not `Int!`) for number field values
- The `clearField` null-path is already parameterized — leave as-is

**Step 5 — Parameterize `setFieldPriority`**
- Named operation: `SetFieldPriority` with variables `$projectId: ID!`, `$itemId: ID!`, `$fieldId: ID!`, `$optionId: String!`
- Same structure as `SetFieldStatus`

**Step 6 — Parameterize `setFieldAssignee`**
- Named operation `ClearAssignees` for the null path: variables `$issueId: ID!`, value `assigneeIds: []`
- Named operation `SetAssignee` for the set path: variables `$issueId: ID!`, `$userId: ID!`
- Note: `issueId` here is an issue node ID (not a project item ID) — this is correct as-is; keep the parameter name `$issueId`

**Step 7 — Verify**
- Run `deno check src/adapters/github/internal/field-value-mutator.ts`
- Confirm no bare template literal mutations remain in the file (`grep '`\`mutation {' field-value-mutator.ts` should return nothing)

- **Unblocks:** F.2.1 (facade wiring), which unblocks #54, #55

# User Story

## Pre-submission check
- [ ] I have searched existing issues and this story is not already tracked.

## As a…
developer

## I want…
to rewrite `BurndownCalculator` from scratch

## So that…
it follows DRY principles and uses existing abstractions

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] File passes `deno check` with no errors
- [ ] `getBurndownInput` uses `PaginatedProjectItemFetcher` from `pagination.ts` — no custom pagination
- [ ] `resolveCompletionTimestamps` reads `response.data` as a direct array — not `response.data.events`
- [ ] Zero `any` types in the file
- [ ] `resolveSprint` and `buildBurndownStoryInput` are imported, not re-implemented

## Story Point Estimate
5

## Affected component
GitHub adapter (src/adapters/github/)

## Additional context / notes
### Why: DRY + Dependency Inversion + eliminating `any`
The three re-implementations (`resolveSprint`, `fetchAllItems`, `buildBurndownStoryInput`) each violate DRY. If the pagination logic or mapping logic changes, `BurndownCalculator` would diverge silently. The correct design: depend on the already-extracted abstractions, not on duplicated copies.

Eliminating `any` at the mapping boundary is required because `buildBurndownStoryInput` in `mappers.ts` already has the correct type for the raw project item — use its input type, not `any`.

### Implementation Steps
**Step 1 — Delete the current file body (keep the header comment)**
- Open `src/adapters/github/internal/burndown-calculator.ts`
- Delete all class body content below the file header comment
- Keep the imports section — it will be rewritten

**Step 2 — Write the correct constructor**
```typescript
import { GitHubClient } from "./http-client.ts";
import { PaginatedProjectItemFetcher } from "./pagination.ts";
import { buildBurndownStoryInput } from "../mappers.ts";
import { resolveSprint } from "./resolver.ts"; // standalone function — not a class method
import type { RuntimeConfig } from "../config-loader.ts";
import type {
  BurndownInput,
  BurndownStoryInput,
  CompletionMap,
  SprintInfo,
} from "../../../scrum/ports.ts";
import type { SprintRef } from "../../../domain/types.ts";

export class BurndownCalculator {
  constructor(
    private readonly config: RuntimeConfig,
    private readonly gh: GitHubClient,
    private readonly owner: string,
    private readonly repo: string,
  ) {}
}
```

**Step 3 — Implement `getBurndownInput(sprint: SprintRef)`**
- Call `resolveSprint(sprint, this.config)` — the standalone function from `resolver.ts`; capture the returned `iterationId: string | null`
- If `iterationId === null`, throw `new Error("Burndown does not apply to the backlog.")`
- Find the iteration entry: `this.config.iterations.all.find((i) => i.id === iterationId)` — throw if not found
- Create a `PaginatedProjectItemFetcher` instance using `this.config`, `{ graphql: this.gh.graphql }`, and appropriate options (same options as `getBacklogStories` in `backend.ts` — include `sprintFieldIds`, `includeIssueContent: true`)
- Call `fetcher.collect()` with a filter predicate that checks `item.fieldValues.nodes` for a field matching `this.config.fields.sprintFieldId` with `iterationId`
- Map filtered items with `buildBurndownStoryInput(item, this.config)` from `mappers.ts`
- Filter out nulls: `.filter((s): s is BurndownStoryInput => s !== null)`
- Compute `endDate` from `iterEntry.startDate + iterEntry.duration` days
- Return `BurndownInput` with `sprint: SprintInfo` and `stories: BurndownStoryInput[]`

**Step 4 — Implement `resolveCompletionTimestamps(input: BurndownInput)`**
- Iterate `input.stories` — for each story with a `number`, call the REST timeline endpoint
- Correct REST path: `repos/${this.owner}/${this.repo}/issues/${story.number}/timeline`
- Correct response shape: `response.data` IS the array — type it as `Array<{ event: string; created_at: string }>`
- Filter for `event === "closed"` where `created_at` falls within `[sprint.startDate, sprint.endDate]`
- Record the last such timestamp in a `Map<number, string>`
- Wrap each story in `try/catch` and `continue` on failure (individual timeline fetch errors should not abort the whole burndown)
- Return `CompletionMap` with `dataSource: "issue_close_proxy"` and the standard warning string

**Step 5 — Verify**
- Run `deno check src/adapters/github/internal/burndown-calculator.ts`
- Confirm no `any` types appear in the file
- Confirm `resolveSprint` is imported from `./resolver.ts`, not defined as a private method
- Confirm `buildBurndownStoryInput` is imported from `../mappers.ts`, not defined as a private method
- Confirm `fetchAllItems` does NOT exist as a method in the class

### Dependencies
- **Depends on:** F.0 (GitHubClient interface)
- **Unblocks:** F.2.1

Domain layer (src/domain/)
